Member spaces: A MEMBER'S PRIVATE ASSISTANT ON A DEVICE SHARED WITH THEIR TEAM (decided by Danny 2026-11-25; not a group chat). THE SPEC of every layer; TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/member-space.ts; web, desktop/CLI, iOS and Android replay the case lists.

DECISIONS: the DEVICE OWNER opts a device in per team, a TEAM OWNER may only switch it off; turns run on the logins ALREADY ON THE DEVICE; on a team device the Assistant works only in the teams that opted that device in; picking a team device starts a NEW conversation, the earlier one stays readable to the member and its key is never handed to the device.

THE OPT-IN: `devices.assistant_team_ids` (uuid[], synced, always a subset of `shared_team_ids`; unsharing a team drops it here too). `devices.setAssistantTeam {deviceId, teamId, allowed}`: allowed true = the device's owner only, the team already shared, kind server, and the device's doctor item `doctorKey` reads `ok` (else PRECONDITION_FAILED with the item's detail); allowed false = the owner, or an owner of that team (`dropAssistantTeam {id, teamId}` on the row id). `optInCases`.

A SPACE is a devices row OF THE MEMBER (user_id = the member, device_id = `space-<uuid>`, kind `server`, label = the host's label) with `space_host_id` (the host's devices row, synced, FK cascade) and `space_team_id` (the team it was picked through). Because it is the member's own device, every existing rule (host, claim, brief, readers) reads it as theirs. At most one per member (`uniq_devices_space_user`). It runs ONLY the trees of the member's Assistant conversation bound to it: every other start, child pick, move, agent, app slot or trigger naming it is refused (`startCases`), it is never a default device, never shared, and no client lists it as a device (Devices page, composer, pickers): clients drop rows with `space_host_id` (`listed`).

PICKING: `memberSpaces.request {deviceId, teamId}` (the host's device_id), in one transaction under the host machine's share lock (`lockDeviceShares`): the caller and the host row's owner are members of teamId, teamId is in assistant_team_ids, the caller does not own the host row; ends a space they have elsewhere (THE END below); creates the row; detaches the running Assistant conversation (status ended, agent_id null, stays readable, exactly as the Assistant move kept the dropped ones) and points the Assistant at the space (`agents.device_id`), its account = null. The next message creates a fresh conversation root there. `agents.update {deviceId}` away from a space ends it; agents.update TO a space or to a foreign shared device is refused: only `request` does it. A fresh request when a space on that host exists is idempotent.

TEAMS: `spaceTeams(hostAssistantTeamIds, hostOwnerTeamIds, memberTeamIds)` = the opted-in teams both belong to NOW, in the member's order (`teamCases`). The Assistant conversation's tree reach (`treeScope`) while its device is a space = its personal team + (its scope today ∩ spaceTeams). Children and chats it starts run in those teams only, on any device that team allows.

THE CREDENTIAL: `memberSpaces.provision {spaceId}` (the host's own account, for a space hosted by its row) answers a fresh API key once, of the MEMBER, metadata {kind: `space`, spaceId}; the earlier key of that space is deleted. parseApiKeyMetadata reads kind `space` (malformed spaceId = grants nothing). Live only while the space row exists. OFF /api/mcp it reaches exactly `procedures` (tRPC paths, everything else FORBIDDEN) and `shapes`, with the member's team set REPLACED by personal + spaceTeams and sessions / messages narrowed to the space's own trees (roots = the Assistant conversations on this space, and sessions whose device is the space); on /api/mcp it is refused (an agent key minted through it is used). A session-argument procedure additionally requires the session to be in a tree of the space. devices.register/heartbeat through it touch only its own row and never kind, sharing, icon, label or default. An agent key minted through it (`users.mintPersonalApiKey`) carries spaceId, is limited to the space's own sessions / personal team + spaceTeams evaluated per request, and dies with the space. mcpServers and skills resolve only for those teams. No space key mints a space key, lists devices of others, approves installs or changes settings.

THE INSTALL: the space's daemon registers an install of kind `installKind` on its space row, through its space key, signed with `registrationLabel` in place of `exp-install-v1` (same lines), so a space install never verifies as an ordinary one. It reads (treeReaders) ONLY the Assistant conversation trees whose root runs on its space; it is in no other tree's reader list, `pending` or public key answer. Approval is the approval kind `approvalKind` (byte `approvalKindByte`), never `approve`; it always asks (the existing-installs rule and a first install never cover it). Until the member's `space` approval verifies, NOBODY wraps for it and the SERVER itself refuses wraps, pending listing and key creation for it. A client pins it as class `space`: it wraps for it, keeps its wraps and accepts its vouch only for a root that is the member's own Assistant conversation (`pinCases`). It can never approve, claim a root, reset or decline. Its code shows on the host with `exponential members`.

WAITING: a conversation on a space whose install is not approved reads `copy.waiting` on the Assistant page and its messages stay queued.

THE END (`endSpacesInTx`, one transaction, `endCases`): causes `unshared`, `optedOut`, `memberLeft`, `ownerLeft`, `deviceRemoved`, `picked` (another device), `installRemoved`, `accountDeleted`, `removed` (the device owner's or a team owner's Remove). A space ends when its spaceTeams is empty or its space_team_id stops being one of them. Its keys (space + agent keys carrying it) are deleted, its install revoked, wraps dropped and the trees due for rotation (#EXP-1951), running sessions of its trees end (the conversation root goes idle), agents.device_id = `` (empty: the page asks for a device, messages stay queued, never a fallback to another device), the row goes. The member gets ONE notification for every cause but `picked` and `accountDeleted`. What the machine already read cannot be taken back.

THE HOST RECONCILES: on start, each heartbeat and each nudge the host's daemon calls `memberSpaces.hosted {deviceId}` ({spaces: [{spaceId, deviceId, member name}]}) and starts / stops child daemons to match; a stopped space first saves unpushed work to refs/exp-wip, then its directory is deleted. No answer (offline) = nothing changes, no new space starts.

ISOLATION: one child daemon per space, data dir `<data>/members/<spaceId>` (0700), in its own user, mount and PID namespaces with no_new_privs: it sees the system read-only, its own directory read-write, a private /tmp and /proc; never the host daemon's data dir or the owner's home, another space, /run/user, /var/run (docker.sock, the session bus), or SSH agents. Environment is an allowlist. The device's logins reach it as access tokens only (no refresh tokens), renewed by the host; no profile directory, transcript or settings of the host is mounted. A machine that cannot do this reports doctor `doctorKey` != ok and cannot be opted in; a space is never started unisolated. Linux servers only.

UI ×4 (existing parts): Settings › Assistant › Runs on lists the member's own machines as before (`runsOnRows`), then per team with opted-in hosts of others a section headed by the TEAM NAME (`spaceSections`, `sectionCases`), rows as ever (offline muted, disabled unless bound); picking one opens the confirm dialog (`copy.pick*`). The bound space shows as its host's row. Device settings › Sharing: under each SHARED team's switch the row `copy.optIn` (disabled with the doctor detail when it cannot), turning on confirms (`copy.optIn*`); then `copy.members`, one row per member with a space here with `copy.remove`. Team owners see the same off switch on the team device they do not own. Needs you shows the install row of install-trust.json, its label the host's label.
